title: A box of gases
hook: Look at the particles before naming the sample.

knows: Atoms of each element are represented by a chemical symbol.
doesNotKnow: A pure element, a pure compound and a mixture differ by particle composition.

misconception: A molecule containing several atoms must be a compound.
objective: Classify a specified particle sample by type and composition.

claims.text: Question, stage and reveal: Each touching group represents one particle. Is this specified sample one pure element, one pure compound, or a mixture of substances? The model contains 2 N₂ and 2 O₂. The two different particle types represent a mixture of substances. Circles show atom counts, not molecular geometry.
claims.source: Specified particle counts and chemical formulas; OpenStax https://openstax.org/books/chemistry-2e/pages/1-2-phases-and-classification-of-matter

claims.text: Atoms are shown as touching circles only to group particles; sizes and geometric arrangement are not molecular structures.
Recall: A sample contains only identical O₂ molecules. How is it classified? All molecules are the same substance and contain only oxygen atoms.

recall.question: A sample contains only identical O₂ molecules. How is it classified?
recall.why: All molecules are the same substance and contain only oxygen atoms.
